viability_note: 28 verified atomic claims. Government spine (ADF&G pages, ADF&G emergency order, NOAA). Killed the intended payoff (c31, the camera did NOT keep the Redoubt count going, the 2025 count ran through the USFS physical weir) and the Bendix dates (c32). Corrections, spelling is Redoubt Lake, 'one of the largest' not 'the largest', the arXiv item is a Feb 2025 preprint not a 2024 paper, drone cadence 'daily' unsupported, UW FRI is one partner not the operator. Keep the three accuracy metrics separate, program 90 percent and 80.2 mAP are self reports, 67.6 mAP (over 90 coho, over 80 sockeye) is the earlier research benchmark.

claims.claim: SalmonVision uses computer vision to automate counting and monitoring of migrating salmon.
claims.quote: Revolutionary computer vision technology enabling precise, automated salmon population monitoring.
claims.softened: Say plainly, computer vision that counts salmon from underwater camera video. Drop the word revolutionary.

claims.claim: Founding organizations are the Pacific Salmon Foundation, the Wild Salmon Center, and Lumax Ecological Analytics.
claims.quote: Founding Organizations: Pacific Salmon Foundation, Wild Salmon Center, Lumax Ecological Analytics

claims.claim: The Sitka Tribe of Alaska is listed as a SalmonVision partner organization.
claims.quote: Sitka Tribe of Alaska

claims.claim: ADF&G is listed among SalmonVision's partner organizations.
claims.quote: Alaska Department of Fish and Game
claims.softened: Say listed among partners, never ADF&G uses SalmonVision.

claims.claim: SalmonVision advertises about 90 percent accuracy for salmon species detection.
claims.quote: 90% Accuracy Rate ... 90%+ accuracy for salmon species detection
claims.softened: Program self report, marketing metric, label it and never conflate with the mAP figures.

claims.claim: SalmonVision reports 80.2 percent mean average precision.
claims.quote: 80.2% ... Mean Average Precision
claims.softened: Program self report, keep separate from the 67.6 research benchmark.

claims.claim: An earlier combined dataset benchmark reached 67.6 percent overall mAP.
claims.quote: achieved a mean average precision (mAP) of 67.6%, and species-specific mAP scores > 90% for coho and > 80% for sockeye salmon
claims.softened: The honest lower research number, label as the earlier benchmark.

claims.claim: Species specific mAP exceeded 90 percent for coho and 80 percent for sockeye on that dataset.
claims.quote: species-specific mAP scores > 90% for coho and > 80% for sockeye salmon

claims.claim: SalmonVision ran at sixteen sites across Alaska and British Columbia in the 2025 season.
claims.quote: In sixteen sites across Alaska and British Columbia this year
claims.softened: 2025 figure, pair with c10's current 20 plus projects.

claims.claim: The program currently states over 20 monitoring projects across BC and Alaska.
claims.quote: over 20 monitoring projects and conservation initiatives across British Columbia and Alaska, with new partnerships emerging in Washington and Oregon for 2026

claims.claim: The Wild Salmon Center aims to scale to 100 watersheds by 2028, a stated goal.
claims.quote: By 2028, the Wild Salmon Center plans to scale its Salmon Vision system to 100 watersheds
claims.softened: A goal, not a result.

claims.claim: The system reportedly processes an hour of video in about one minute.
claims.quote: The Salmon Vision system can process an hour of video in one minute.
claims.softened: Program reported performance, say reportedly.

claims.claim: The model is trained on over 5 million annotated frames, the program's current figure.
claims.quote: Trained on over 5 million annotated frames

claims.claim: Hardware builds that once cost upward of 50,000 dollars now reportedly run about 10,000 with edge processing.
claims.quote: Builds that used to cost upward of $50k now run $10k for a video box with edge processing system, and $5k for a video system alone.
claims.softened: Program reported costs relayed by an independent outlet.

claims.claim: A video only rig reportedly runs about 5,000 dollars.
claims.quote: $5k for a video system alone

claims.claim: Redoubt Lake supports one of the largest sockeye subsistence fisheries in Southeast Alaska.
claims.quote: In Redoubt Lake, one of the largest sockeye salmon fisheries in southeast Alaska
claims.softened: One of the largest, and the spelling is Redoubt.

claims.claim: The US Forest Service announced in February 2024 it no longer had funds to operate the Redoubt Lake weir.
claims.quote: the U.S. Forest Service ... announced in February 2024 that it no longer had funds to operate the weir at the Redoubt Lake outlet
claims.softened: Sentinel page blocks automated fetch, captured via snippet and corroborated by the ADF&G release (c19).

claims.claim: The Sitka Tribe stepped in to support management at Redoubt with a 200,000 dollar tribal wildlife grant, proposing AI enabled video with the Wild Salmon Center and the Forest Service.
claims.quote: STA currently is supporting management at Redoubt
claims.softened: Stepped in to support management, the AI video piece is a grant funded proposal, not a completed replacement.

claims.claim: The Redoubt Lake weir, operated by the US Forest Service, was operational June 14, 2025 and had counted 8,111 sockeye by June 29, 2025.
claims.quote: The Redoubt Lake weir, operated by the U.S. Forest Service, was installed and operational on June 14, 2025 ... As of June 29, 8,111 sockeye salmon have been counted through the weir
claims.softened: The reality check, the 2025 count came through the physical weir, not an AI camera.

claims.claim: ADF&G uses weirs and counting towers in clear narrow streams, which do not work in wide turbid rivers.
claims.quote: Traditional tools such as weirs and counting towers can be used to count salmon in clear, narrow streams or tributaries, but not in wide, turbid rivers.

claims.claim: ADF&G uses imaging sonar (DIDSON and ARIS) to detect and count fish in rivers.
claims.quote: When the Alaska Department of Fish and Game adopted Dual frequency IDentification SONar (DIDSON) as a tool for detecting fish, inriver fisheries sonar advanced a giant leap forward.

claims.claim: ARIS was first tested in Alaska in 2012.
claims.quote: The latest generation of imaging sonar technology, known as ARIS (Adaptive Resolution Imaging Sonar), was first tested in Alaska in 2012.

claims.claim: Counting fish with DIDSON or ARIS requires a technician watching video and counting fish images, labor and time intensive.
claims.quote: a technician watching DIDSON or ARIS video counts images of swimming fish ... Reviewing data and manually measuring individual fish is both labor and time intensive.
claims.softened: The honest humans-still-count-today anchor, lead with it.

claims.claim: A February 2025 arXiv preprint reports about a 23 percent count error on representative Kenai River sonar data, framed as demonstrating feasibility.
claims.quote: We achieve a count error of 23% on representative data from the Kenai River in Alaska, demonstrating the feasibility of our approach.
claims.softened: A preprint, not peer reviewed, and never invert into 77 percent accurate.

claims.claim: NOAA's Alaska Fisheries Science Center customized YOLOv11 to detect pollock and salmon in fishing nets.
claims.quote: Scientists at the Alaska Fisheries Science Center customized it to detect and identify both pollock and salmon in fishing nets.
claims.softened: Adjacent Alaska fisheries AI example, bycatch review, not weir counting.

claims.claim: NOAA's models process fishing tows in hours versus days to weeks for human review.
claims.quote: They can process fishing tows in a matter of hours; humans would need days to weeks to review the same data.

claims.claim: A Bristol Bay drone salmon counting research project on the Wood River counts UW's Fisheries Research Institute among its partners.
claims.quote: the University of Washington's Fisheries Research Institute ... It's one of the partners supporting this research, alongside Bristol Bay Regional Seafood Development Association and Bristol Bay Economic Development Corporation.
claims.softened: One partner among several, not the sole operator.

claims.claim: An autonomous drone flies a programmed morning path to observe salmon over the Wood River.
claims.quote: It quickly takes off on an automated flight path, flying to an observation position above the right bank of the Wood River.
claims.softened: No daily cadence stated, do not say daily.

claims.claim: The drone project is early stage and will test its models against Fish and Game tower counts in a next phase.
claims.quote: The crew will test their models against Fish & Game tower counting data in the project's next phase.
claims.softened: Validation is a next phase plan, not a result.

claims.claim: Dr William Atlas of the Wild Salmon Center said video weirs reduce migration delays dramatically compared with traditional trap associated weirs.
claims.quote: Video weirs tend to reduce migration delays fairly dramatically, when compared to sort of traditional trap-associated weirs.
claims.softened: Attribute exactly, Dr William Atlas, Wild Salmon Center senior salmon watershed scientist.

claims.claim: KILLED. The camera kept the Redoubt count going after the tribe took over.
claims.quote: (no supporting sentence exists on the page)
claims.softened: Contradicted by c19, the 2025 count ran through the USFS physical weir. AI video at Redoubt is a proposal (c18). Never use this payoff.

claims.claim: KILLED. DIDSON replaced Bendix sonar across sites 2002 to 2011.
claims.quote: (page does not mention Bendix or a 2002-2011 window)
